transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I'm here because my head just feels a bit foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things. 

Um... like appointment times, or the dates for the exhibits. Or I'll forget which volunteer I already called. Just... having some trouble keeping things straight, I guess.
Are these memory problems making it hard for you to manage your usual daily activities on your own?

Well... I suppose so. It's... it's been a little difficult. I did miss a few of my own doctor visits recently. And the schedule at the senior center got pretty tangled up. 

My husband... well, he's had to step in lately. He helps with the phone calls now, and keeping the calendars straight. Even handling decisions about house repairs that I always used to take care of myself. So... yes, I guess I'm not managing it all on my own right now.
Have there been times when your confusion comes on suddenly or seems to fluctuate a lot during the day?
I... no, I don't think so. It doesn't really come and go suddenly like that. It's just... mostly the same, I suppose. Just a steady sort of fog.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
No, I... I wouldn't say that. I don't feel depressed. Just... tired, maybe. But not down.
Have you been diagnosed with a medical condition that your doctors think is causing these memory problems?
I... no. Not that they've told me. Nobody has mentioned any specific condition causing it. Just... no.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?
I... not really. I mean, sometimes I pause, but... no, I don't think I have trouble finding words. Just... normal talking, I guess.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious or worried lately?
No... I don't think so. I don't really worry too much. Just... the usual, I suppose. Nothing unusual.
Have these memory problems been gradually getting worse over time?
I... I'm not really sure. I don't know if they're getting worse. It's just... hard to tell. I haven't really been keeping track.
Have your doctors ever told you that memory testing showed a problem with your thinking or memory?
No... I don't recall anyone ever saying that to me. I don't think I've had any tests like that... not that I remember, anyway.
Have you gotten lost in places that used to be familiar to you?
No... I don't think so. I usually just go to the same places, so... I haven't gotten lost, no.
Has your husband told you that he has noticed your memory or thinking getting worse?
No... he hasn't said anything to me about it. We don't really... talk about that sort of thing. He hasn't mentioned anything.
Has anyone close to you noticed that your memory has gotten worse?
No... nobody's said anything like that to me. I mostly just keep to myself anyway, so... no, I don't think so.
Has your husband noticed your memory problems?
No... like I said, he hasn't mentioned anything to me. I don't think he's noticed anything different.
Has a doctor ever told you that you have dementia?
No... no doctor has ever said anything like that to me.
Has any doctor or nurse told you that a memory test showed problems with your thinking?
No... I haven't ever taken a test like that. So... no, they haven't.
Have you had trouble managing your medications on your own?
No... I manage them just fine. I haven't had any trouble with that.
Have you ever had a memory or thinking test that showed a problem?
I thought you just... no. Like I said a minute ago, I haven't taken any tests for my memory. So, no.
Has any doctor ever told you that you have mild cognitive impairment?
No... nobody has ever said that to me. I haven't heard those words before.
Has a doctor ever done a memory test that showed a problem?
I... didn't I just answer that? No. Like I told you, no doctor has done any memory tests on me.
Has your husband ever told a doctor that your memory has been getting worse?
My husband? No... he hasn't. He hasn't said anything like that to anyone.
